session.question: How can the Paris Agreement be used in makin�27 healthcare or manufacturing teams push more sustainable practices, and what do the three I's say about why policy coherence with it can be helped or hindered?
session.answer:
The Paris Agreement serves as a critical framework for encouraging healthcare and manufacturing teams to adopt sustainable practices. By aligning operational strategies with the Agreement's objectives, these sectors can integrate climate change considerations into their practices, as emphasized in studies advocating for eco-conscious approaches within healthcare (unknownauthorsUnknownyearadvancingsustainablehealthcare chunk 1). The Agreement's emphasis on collaborative action promotes a culture of environmental responsibility, urging healthcare professionals and industry actors to innovate and implement sustainable measures (unknownauthorsUnknownyearsustainablehealthcare– chunk 1, unknownauthorsUnknownyearcirculareconomyin chunk 1). 

However, achieving policy coherence is complex, as outlined by the three I's—ideas, institutions, and interests. Ideas reflect the ideologies that shape perceptions of sustainability; institutions encompass the formal and informal rules governing behavior. Interests pertain to the vested motivations of actors involved in the policy-making process. This interplay can facilitate or obstruct coherent implementation depending on how well these elements align with the goals of the Paris Agreement (unknownauthorsUnknownyearpoliticaldriversof chunk 1). Specifically, entrenched interests may resist changes that threaten established practices, while supportive institutions and innovative ideas can foster a conducive environment for integrating sustainability into both healthcare and manufacturing sectors (unknownauthorsUnknownyearaligningclimateand chunk 1).

The Paris Agreement serves as a critical framework for encouraging healthcare and manufacturing teams to adopt sustainable practices. By aligning operational strategies with the Agreement's objectives, these sectors can integrate climate change considerations into their practices, as emphasized in studies advocating for eco-conscious approaches within healthcare (unknownauthorsUnknownyearadvancingsustainablehealthcare chunk 1). The Agreement's emphasis on collaborative action promotes a culture of environmental responsibility, urging healthcare professionals and industry actors to innovate and implement sustainable measures (unknownauthorsUnknownyearsustainablehealthcare– chunk 1, unknownauthorsUnknownyearcirculareconomyin chunk 1). 

However, achieving policy coherence is complex, as outlined by the three I's—ideas, institutions, and interests. Ideas reflect the ideologies that shape perceptions of sustainability; institutions encompass the formal and informal rules governing behavior. Interests pertain to the vested motivations of actors involved in the policy-making process. This interplay can facilitate or obstruct coherent implementation depending on how well these elements align with the goals of the Paris Agreement (unknownauthorsUnknownyearpoliticaldriversof chunk 1). Specifically, entrenched interests may resist changes that threaten established practices, while supportive institutions and innovative ideas can foster a conducive environment for integrating sustainability into both healthcare and manufacturing sectors (unknownauthorsUnknownyearaligningclimateand chunk 1).
